identity.name: Teutonic Order
alt_names: monastic state of the Teutonic Knights

land.text: Chełmno Land (Culmerland), 'granting them Chełmno Land, or Culmerland, and any future conquests' (Golden Bull of Rimini, 1226)

predecessors.note: The Prussian Crusade page: 'With the permission of Duke Conrad of Masovia and the Masovian nobility, Christian requested aid from the Teutonic Order against the Prussians in 1226.' The rest of Prussia was taken from the stateless Prussian tribes (counterpart 'nobody').

land.text: the Swordbrothers' lands in Livonia, absorbed in 1237

predecessors.note: Joined 1237 ('most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order'), seven years after the state's start; Cliopatria keeps the Swordbrothers' own row to 1240.

land.text: the Order's remaining Prussian territories, secularized by Albert of Brandenburg

successors.note: Prussian Homage 10 April 1525: Albert 'resigned and converted to Lutheranism, becoming Duke of Prussia as a vassal of Poland'.

land.text: the Livonian branch's lands (Latvia and Estonia)

successors.note: Not an end-of-life succession: Cliopatria detaches Livonia from the Teutonic Order in 1422; the Livonian Order stayed a 'semi-autonomous branch' of the Order until 1561.

capitals.name: Marienburg (Malbork)
capitals.note: State page infobox 'Marienburg (1308-1454)'; the Order page gives 1309-1466 and the Thirteen Years' War page has the castle handed to the Polish army on 6 June 1457 (the pages disagree; see notes). Acre (1190-1291) and Venice (1291-1309) were the Order's headquarters outside Prussia and lie outside every shape of this state, so they are not listed as capitals (review 2026-10-25); no page opened (Teutonic Order, State of the Teutonic Order, Prussian crusade, Hermann Balk, Grand Master) names a seat of the Prussian state before 1309.

capitals.name: Königsberg (Kaliningrad)
capitals.note: State page infobox 'Königsberg (1454-1525)'; the Order page gives 1466 for the move.

rulers.name: Hermann von Salza
rulers.title: Grand Master
rulers.note: Grand Master 1209-1239 (the state starts in 1230). Until 1309 the Grand Masters sat in Acre and Venice, outside Prussia; the Landmeister governed Prussia (the page opened does not mention the office).

rulers.name: Albert of Brandenburg-Ansbach
rulers.title: Grand Master
rulers.note: last Grand Master of the Prussian state; he turned it into the Duchy of Prussia (10 April 1525)

correction.text: Chełmno Land: 'By 1232, the Knights had established or rebuilt fortresses at Culm (Chełmno) and Thorn' (Prussian Crusade page); granted to the Order by the Golden Bull of Rimini, 1226

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Teutonic shape begins in 1236 but the State page's infobox gives 'Sovereign state (1230-1466)' and says 'The Knights began the Prussian Crusade in 1230'; the Golden Bull of Rimini (1226) had given them Chełmno Land. The 1236 shape (Chełmno Land, 3,982 km2) is used for 1230-1235.

correction.text: Chełmno Land as drawn (3,982 km2), valid for 1236 only; the Swordbrothers' lands join in 1237 (keyframe teutonic-order_1237)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1236 shape is Chełmno Land to 1240. It is right for 1236 only: the Livonian Order page dates the merger of the Swordbrothers to 1237 ('most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order'), so the Livonian lands are not the Order's in 1236 (the livonian-brothers-of-the-sword dossier draws them to 1237). The Pomesanian submission of 1236 (ledger) adds Prussian land that the shape does not show. (Review 2026-10-25: the earlier version added the Livonian lands from 1236; split into this keyframe and teutonic-order_1237.)

correction.text: Chełmno Land plus, from 1237, the lands of the Livonian Brothers of the Sword ('absorbed by the Teutonic Knights in 1237')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Livonian Order page says 'most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order' in 1237 (after Saule, 1236), so from 1237 the Livonian lands (Cliopatria's Livonian Brothers shape of 1237, 68,087 km2) belong to the Order. Cliopatria draws only Chełmno Land (3,982 km2) to 1240, keeps the Livonian lands under the Swordbrothers' row to 1240 and gives them to the Order from 1241; the 1237 merger is ledger event 1237. The Pomesanian submission of 1236 and the 1238-40 campaigns against Bartians, Natangians and Warmians (Prussian Crusade page) add Prussian land that the shape does not show.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape without the Pskov and Leningrad oblast land, which no page gives to the Order (Pskov was taken in September 1240 by Prince Yaroslav 'and the men from the bishopric of Dorpat' and Alexander 'managed to retake both Votia and Pskov' in the campaign of 1241)

keyframe_review.note: 93,820 km2: Livonia plus the Prussian lands then held. The shape reaches Pskov and Leningrad oblasts (54 cells, about 12,000 km2). Battle on the Ice page: Pskov fell in September 1240 to Prince Yaroslav Vladimirovich with 'the men from the bishopric of Dorpat'; 'in the winter of 1240-41, a group of Latin Christians invaded Votia' (Koporye; the page does not name who held it); 'During the campaign of 1241, Alexander managed to retake both Votia and Pskov'; the battle of 5 April 1242 'prevented the crusaders from retaking Pskov'; the 1242 terms in the Novgorod First Chronicle have the Germans withdraw from the land of the Vod, Luga, Pskov and Latgale. None of this has the Order itself holding the land, and Alexander's recapture is dated 1241, so the cells are dropped from 1241 and the former ledger loss of 1242 (counterpart novgorod-republic) is deleted: keyframe and ledger now agree. Disagreement with the review of 2026-10-25, which read the page as the Order holding Pskov 1240-1242 and offered a new 1241-1242 keyframe as the alternative to deleting the loss. Sizes: the Terra Mariana page gives the Livonian Order about 67,000 km2 by the mid-14th century, so the Livonian part of the shape (about 70,000 km2) is within a factor of two.

96,155 km2 for 1250-1254: the Treaty of Christburg (February 1249) brought 'most of the' Prussian tribes to peace, matching Cliopatria's jump in Warmia and Masuria (97 of 108 cells). From January 1255 Samland is added (new keyframe 1255); the shape's remaining years 1255-1259 are replaced by it.

correction.text: the 1250 shape plus Samland (the Sambian peninsula)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Samland was conquered in January 1255 in a campaign lasting less than a month'. Cliopatria's 1250 shape has 13 of the 62 Kaliningrad-oblast cells and its 1260 shape has 61; the 1255 shape adds Samland (Sambia, the peninsula around Königsberg) to the 1250 shape. Other jumps between the two shapes (Natangia, Nadruvia, Skalvia) are not dated by the page.

112,647 km2 with 61 of 62 Kaliningrad-oblast cells. The Great Prussian Uprising began the same year ('The native victory inspired the Prussians to rebel again, starting the Great Prussian uprising the same year'), so the shape shows the Order's claim, not the ground it held; the page gives no map of rebel-held land and says only 'The central Prussian tribes surrendered to the crusaders by 1277'. Sudovia (1283) was 'left unpopulated, becoming a border wilderness' and is not in the shape.

112,373 km2: the same lands after the uprising; the only change from 1260 is two Lithuanian-border cells. 'The crusaders firmly controlled the Prussian tribes by the end of the 13th century' (later uprisings in 1286 and 1295).
112,395 km2, no Pomerelia. Right for 1305-1308; Gdańsk fell on 13 November 1308 and the Treaty of Soldin followed in September 1309, so 1309-1313 is a new keyframe.

New keyframe: 'In September 1309, Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg-Stendal sold his claim to the territory to the Teutonic Order for 10,000 marks in the Treaty of Soldin'; the Order 'seized all of Pomerelia (Gdańsk Pomerania)' after taking Gdańsk on 13 November 1308. Cliopatria adds Pomerelia only in 1314 (71 of 86 Pomorskie cells).
128,584 km2 with Pomerelia, which the Order held from 1308-1309; Cliopatria starts it in 1314.
142,726 km2 including Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land, 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' and given back at Kalisz on 8 July 1343. Cliopatria shows them 1333-1343 as drawn.
130,387 km2: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń returned to Poland at Kalisz (8 July 1343). Right for 1344-1345; the Duchy of Estonia is added in 1346 (new keyframe).

correction.text: the Order's lands with the Duchy of Estonia bought in 1346

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1346, the Duchy of Estonia was sold by the King of Denmark for 19,000 Cologne marks to the Teutonic Order' (the Livonian Order page: 'In 1346, the order bought the Duchy of Estonia from King Valdemar IV of Denmark'). The Danish Estonia page dates the shift of sovereignty to 1 November 1346. Cliopatria adds the Estonian cells (111 to 170) only in 1352; this keyframe is its 1352 shape from 1346.

144,577 km2 for 1352-1397. The Order's state had about 220,000 inhabitants at the start of the 14th century (State page); no area figure is given for it, so only the Livonian part could be checked (see 1241).

correction.text: the 1402 shape (with Gotland and Samogitia) without the Neumark, which came in 1402

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Order conquered the island [Gotland] in 1398 after Albert of Sweden had pledged it to them' (Order page); the State page's table gives Samogitia 1398-1411. Cliopatria adds both only in 1402 together with the Neumark; the Neumark was pawned to the Order in 1402, so 1398-1401 is the 1402 shape without it.

correction.text: valid for 1402-1407; the Neumark (pawned 1402), Gotland (1398) and Samogitia (1398) are all inside

keyframe_review.note: 192,255 km2, the Order's largest shape; the Order page says it 'reached its greatest territorial extent in 1407'. Right for 1402-1407. Gotland was sold in 1408 and Samogitia resigned in 1411, so 1408-1410 and 1411-1414 are new keyframes; Cliopatria keeps both to 1414.
New keyframe: the State page's table gives Gotland 1398-1408 and the text says the Order sold it to Denmark ('Letzkau arranged that the Order sell Gotland to Denmark').

correction.text: the Order's lands without Samogitia (and without Gotland)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Peace of Thorn of 1 February 1411: the Knights 'agreed to resign their claims to Samogitia during the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas' and 'ceded the Dobrin Land'. Cliopatria drops Samogitia in 1415; this keyframe is its 1415 shape from 1411.

150,857 km2: Prussia with the Neumark, Pomerelia and Livonia (the branch is still inside the Order's shape until 1421). The Hunger War of 1414 and the Gollub War of 1422 are named without territorial change.

68,810 km2: Prussia and the Neumark; the Livonian branch (Latvia, Estonia) is a separate Cliopatria row from 1422. The Treaty of Melno (27 September 1422) settled the Lithuanian frontier: 'Samogitia was permanently ceded to Lithuania', a frontier that 'remained unchanged for about 500 years'. Right for 1422-1454; the Neumark leaves in 1455 (new keyframe).

correction.text: the Order's Prussia without the Neumark

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'In 1454 and 1455, the Teutonic Knights first pawned, then sold the Neumark back to the' Brandenburg margraviate. This keyframe is Cliopatria's 1459 shape from 1455.

62,530 km2: the Order's claim to all of Prussia without the Neumark. The war front moved: the Prussian Confederation held western Prussia from 1454, the Poles took Marienburg town on 5 July 1460, 'Teutonic forces then regained western Prussian towns', so the western land is contested (ledger contest events), not simply the Order's.

correction.text: the Order's Prussia as claimed until the Peace of Thorn; the western land is the contest zone

keyframe_review.note: 42,660 km2: Cliopatria removes Pomerelia and Chełmno in 1463, but the Thirteen Years' War page has Mewe (Gniew) besieged from 27 July 1463 and capitulating on 1 January 1464 and Konitz falling on 28 September 1466, and the treaty that gave the land up was signed on 19 October 1466. So 1463-1465 keeps the 1459 shape (as a contested zone) and the 1468 shape starts in 1466 (new keyframe).

correction.text: the Order's eastern Prussia, a fief of the Polish Crown

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Second Peace of Thorn, 19 October 1466: the Order 'renounced any claims to the territories of Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and Chełmno Land', Elbing and Marienburg 'were also recognized as part of Poland', 'The eastern part remained with the Teutonic Order as a fief of the Polish Crown'; the Thirteen Years' War page adds 'The Bishopric of Warmia also came under the Polish crown'. This keyframe is Cliopatria's 1468 shape from 1466.

38,410 km2: eastern Prussia without Warmia; the Order is a Polish fief ('every Grand Master of the Teutonic Order was obliged to swear an oath of allegiance to the reigning Polish king within six months of taking office').
38,518 km2: the same land (a difference of about 100 km2). No page opened dates a border change in the Order's last decades; the War of the Priests (1467-1479) was over the bishops of Warmia.

38,518 km2 for 1521-1525, equal to Cliopatria's first Duchy of Prussia shape (1526). The Order's Prussian branch ends with the Prussian Homage on 10 April 1525 when Albert of Brandenburg 'resigned and converted to Lutheranism, becoming Duke of Prussia as a vassal of Poland'.

ledger.note: 1230: the Teutonic Knights begin the Prussian Crusade from Chełmno Land, granted to them by the Golden Bull of Rimini. The State page infobox reads 'Sovereign state (1230-1466)' and 'The Knights began the Prussian Crusade in 1230'; 'the Golden Bull of Rimini in 1226 and the Papal Bull of Rieti of 1234' gave them Prussia. The land is the 1236 Cliopatria shape.

1236: the Knights force most Pomesanians to submit. 'the crusaders advanced north along both banks of the Vistula and forced the submission of most Pomesanians'; the fortress at Marienwerder (Kwidzyn) dates from summer 1233. Pomesania is not in the gazetteer, so a radius round Kwidzyn stands for it.

1237: the Livonian Brothers of the Sword merge into the Teutonic Order. 'most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order' after their defeat at Saule in 1236; 'Between 1237 and 1290, the Livonian Order conquered all of Courland, Livonia and Semigallia' (the page gives no dated conquest steps inside that span).

region.text: Warmia, Natangia and Bartia, the tribes that made peace at Christburg

ledger.note: February 1249: the Treaty of Christburg brings most Prussian tribes to peace. 'most of the latter agreed to peace in the Treaty of Christburg in February 1249', after the 1233-34 Pogesanian and 1238-40 Bartian, Natangian and Warmian campaigns. The land is read as Warmia and the Masurian lands (Cliopatria: 33 to 97 cells there by 1250).
January 1255: the Knights conquer Samland. 'Samland was conquered in January 1255 in a campaign lasting less than a month'; Königsberg was founded during it, named for the Bohemian king.

By 1277 the central Prussian tribes have surrendered. 'The central Prussian tribes surrendered to the crusaders by 1277' after the Great Prussian Uprising that began in 1260; the page gives no end date for the uprising, and says 'the crusaders firmly controlled the Prussian tribes by the end of the 13th century'.

13 November 1308: the Teutonic Knights take Gdańsk and with it Pomerelia. Gdańsk 'was captured by the State of the Teutonic Order on 13 November 1308' and the order 'seized all of Pomerelia (Gdańsk Pomerania)'; the page names Polish rulers (Przemysł II, Władysław I) as nominal overlords and says Brandenburg held the west.

1309: the Order's seat moves from Venice to Marienburg, the first seat of the Order inside the state's land. 'they moved from Venice to Marienburg (Malbork) on the Nogat River after gaining Pomerelia' (Order page infobox Marienburg 1309-1466; the State page gives 1308). Acre and Venice are not capitals of this state (see identity.capitals).

region.text: the Brandenburg claim to Pomerelia, sold at Soldin

ledger.note: September 1309: Brandenburg sells its claim to Pomerelia. 'In September 1309, Margrave Waldemar of Brandenburg-Stendal sold his claim to the territory to the Teutonic Order for 10,000 marks in the Treaty of Soldin'; the Order page says the castles of Gdańsk, Świecie and Tczew were purchased.

region.text: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land, conquered by the Order between 1329 and 1332

ledger.note: 1329: the Order attacks Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land in the Polish-Teutonic War. The Kalisz page: the land was 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332'; the war 'began in 1326/1327'. The first year of conquest is the page's; the exact first campaign is not given.
1332: Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land are in the Order's hands. They were 'conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332' and held to the Treaty of Kalisz of 1343; the war itself ended only then.
1332: the Order's conquest of Kuyavia and Dobrzyń is complete; the land is held, not fought over, until the 1343 peace. The page gives 1332 as the end of the conquest, not of the war.

region.text: Danish Estonia: Harria and Vironia, with Reval and Wesenberg

ledger.note: 16 May 1343: the Order takes the castles of Reval and Wesenberg in Danish Estonia. 'The castles in Reval and Wesenberg were handed over to the Order by the pro-German party on 16 May 1343', after the St George's Night Uprising of 1343; the castle at Narva followed in 1345. Denmark kept the sovereignty until the sale.

8 July 1343: the Treaty of Kalisz returns Kuyavia and Dobrzyń to Poland. The treaty 'regained Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land, which had been conquered by the Teutonic Order between 1329 and 1332'; King Casimir III 'undertook to raise no future claims on Pomerelia, as well as Chełmno Land and Michałów Land'.
1 November 1346: the contest over Estonia ends with the sale. 'The shift of sovereignty from Denmark to the Teutonic Order took place on 1 November 1346.'

region.text: the Duchy of Estonia (Harria and Vironia)

ledger.note: 1 November 1346: the Order buys the Duchy of Estonia from Denmark. 'In 1346, Estonia (Harria and Vironia) was sold for 19,000 Cologne marks to the Teutonic Order'; sovereignty shifted on 1 November 1346. The State page: 'In 1346, the Duchy of Estonia was sold by the King of Denmark'; the Livonian Order page: 'the order bought the Duchy of Estonia from King Valdemar IV of Denmark'. The seller is the Danish crown; Cliopatria's Danish Estonia row is 'Danish Magnates'.

1398: the Order takes Gotland from the Victual Brothers. 'King Albert of Sweden ceded Gotland to the Order as a pledge' and 'An invasion force under Grand Master Konrad von Jungingen conquered the island in 1398', which 'drove the Victual Brothers out of Gotland' (Teutonic Order page); the Victual Brothers page: they 'occupied the island of Gotland, Sweden, in 1394 and set up their headquarters in Visby' and the Order 'conquered the island in 1398, destroying Visby'. Counterpart is the occupier, not Sweden: Albert (the Mecklenburg king, deposed 1389) was no longer a ruling king, and kingdom-of-sweden has no life in 1398 (merged into kalmar-union in June 1397). The State page's table gives Gotland 1398-1408. (Review 2026-10-25: counterpart was kingdom-of-sweden.)

12 October 1398: the Treaty of Salynas gives Samogitia to the Order. Signed 'on 12 October 1398' by Vytautas and Grand Master Konrad von Jungingen; Samogitia went to the Knights 'roughly up to the Nevėžis River', and the Order 'also received a portion of Sudovia for the first time' (Treaty of Salynas page; the Sudovian part is not drawn). The State page's table gives 'Samogitia | 1398-1411'; the Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War page says it was 'in Teutonic hands since the Peace of Raciąż of 1404', which the Salynas page now explains (the 1404 peace confirmed it; the Raciąż page did not load). (Review 2026-10-25: date was year-only, confidence 2, from the State page.)

region.text: the Neumark, the part of Brandenburg east of the Oder

ledger.note: 1402: the Neumark is pawned to the Order. Table 'Neumark | 1402-1455'; 'the Luxembourgs gave the region in pawn to the Teutonic Order'. Counterpart is the Brandenburg margraviate (Sigismund of Luxembourg was its margrave).

1408: the Order sells Gotland to Denmark. Table 'Gotland | 1398-1408'; 'Letzkau arranged that the Order sell Gotland to Denmark'. Denmark's Cliopatria row ended in 1406 and the Danish king ruled the Kalmar Union from 1407, so the counterpart is the union.
May 1409: Samogitia rises against the Order. 'In May 1409, an uprising in Teutonic-held Samogitia started'; the Grand Master declared war on Poland and Lithuania on 6 August 1409.

region.text: Samogitia, resigned for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas

ledger.note: 1 February 1411: the First Peace of Thorn gives up Samogitia. The Knights 'agreed to resign their claims to Samogitia during the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas' and 'ceded the Dobrin Land' to Poland (Dobrzyń is not drawn in Cliopatria's shape). The war included Grunwald (15 July 1410).
1 February 1411: the Peace of Thorn ends the fighting over Samogitia. 'The Peace of Thorn was signed on 1 February 1411'; 'Territorial disputes lasted until the Peace of Melno of 1422'.

region.text: the Livonian branch's lands in Latvia and Estonia

ledger.note: 1422: Cliopatria sets the Livonian branch apart as its own state. The Treaty of Melno (27 September 1422) gave Samogitia 'permanently' to Lithuania and the Samogitian strip 'separated the Teutonic Knights in Prussia from their branch in Livonia'; the Terra Mariana page calls the branch 'semi-autonomous' from 1237 and the Livonian Confederation agreement is dated Walk, 4 December 1435. No opened page dates a 1422 separation; the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Nieszawa and half of the Vistula channel

ledger.note: 27 September 1422: the Treaty of Melno gives Nieszawa to Poland. 'The Kingdom of Poland received Nieszawa and half of the Vistula channel from the mouth of the Drwęca River'; the Order's castle at Nieszawa was to be demolished. The page does not say the Order ceded it.

1454: the Order's seat moves from Marienburg to Königsberg. State page infobox 'Marienburg (1308-1454) Königsberg (1454-1525)'; the Order page gives 1466 and the Thirteen Years' War page has the castle handed to the Polish army on 6 June 1457.

region.text: western Prussia, which became the Polish province of Royal Prussia

ledger.note: February-March 1454: the Prussian Confederation rises and western Prussia turns to the Polish king. 'Two days later the confederacy started its rebellion' (after 4 February 1454); delegates pledged allegiance to Casimir IV on 6 March 1454 (the Order's western Prussia: Chełmno, Pomerelia, Elbing, Marienburg).

1455: the Order sells the Neumark back to Brandenburg. 'In 1454 and 1455, the Teutonic Knights first pawned, then sold the Neumark back to the' Brandenburg margraviate (Treaties of Cölln and Mewe); the Order page: it 'returned it to Brandenburg in 1455 to raise war funds'.

region.text: the castles of Marienburg, Dirschau and Eylau

ledger.note: 6 June 1457: Marienburg passes to the Poles. 'On 6 June 1457, the castles of Marienburg, Dirschau, and Eylau were transferred to the Polish army.' The Poles took Marienburg town on 5 July 1460 and the Order regained some western towns afterwards, so the loss is not final until 1466.

19 October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn ends the Thirteen Years' War. 'signed in the Hanseatic city of Thorn (Toruń) on 19 October 1466' (the war page's text says 10 October, its infobox 19 October).

region.text: Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania, Chełmno Land, the region of Elbing and Marienburg

ledger.note: 19 October 1466: the Order gives up western Prussia. 'the Teutonic Order renounced any claims to the territories of Gdańsk/Eastern Pomerania and Chełmno Land'; 'the region of Elbing (Elbląg) and Marienburg (Malbork)' were also recognised as part of Poland (Royal Prussia). 'The eastern part remained with the Teutonic Order as a fief of the Polish Crown.'

1466: the Bishopric of Warmia passes to the Polish crown. 'The Bishopric of Warmia also came under the Polish crown'; the Prince-Bishop Paul von Legensdorf joined Poland in 1466. Cliopatria removes Warmia from the Order's shape only in 1468.

region.text: the eastern part of Prussia that 'remained with the Teutonic Order as a fief of the Polish Crown'

ledger.note: 19 October 1466: the Order becomes a fief of the Polish Crown. 'The eastern part remained with the Teutonic Order as a fief of the Polish Crown' (page: treaty signed in Thorn 'on 19 October 1466'); the Grand Master swore the Polish king an oath of allegiance (see keyframe teutonic-order_1468). Mirrors house-of-jagiellon ledger 1466-10 vassal_start (counterpart teutonic-order). (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

region.text: the Order's Prussian state as a fief of Poland

ledger.note: 10 April 1525: the Order's fief ends in the Prussian Homage. 'Prussian Homage (end of the Prussian branch): 10 April 1525'; Albert's submission to Poland 'became known as the Prussian Homage' and the land, 'Ducal Prussia', stayed 'a Polish fief' under a secular duke (the Second Peace of Thorn page: Albert became hereditary duke 'under the overlordship of Poland in the Prussian Homage'). The fief continues as duchy-of-prussia; house-of-jagiellon ledger 1525-4 has vassal_end for teutonic-order and vassal_start for duchy-of-prussia. (Added 2026-10-25 on review.)

region.text: the Order's remaining Prussian territories, secularized

ledger.note: 10 April 1525: the Order's Prussian state ends in the Prussian Homage. 'Prussian Homage (end of the Prussian branch): 10 April 1525'; Grand Master Albert of Brandenburg 'resigned and converted to Lutheranism, becoming Duke of Prussia as a vassal of Poland' and secularized the remaining Prussian lands.

wars.name: Prussian Crusade
belligerents: Old Prussian tribes (Pomesanians, Pogesanians, Warmians, Natangians, Bartians, Sambians, Sudovians)

zones.text: Prussia east of the Vistula, conquered tribe by tribe

wars.outcome: The Order conquered Prussia: Pomesania in 1233-36, the central tribes' peace at Christburg in February 1249, Samland in January 1255, the Great Prussian Uprising from 1260, Sudovia in summer 1283; 'the crusaders firmly controlled the Prussian tribes by the end of the 13th century'.
wars.note: The Prussian Crusade page puts the conquest at 'more than fifty years' (Order page). Later uprisings in 1286 and 1295.

wars.name: Great Prussian uprising
wars.outcome: Crushed: 'The central Prussian tribes surrendered to the crusaders by 1277'.
wars.note: The page gives the start (1260, after the 'native victory') but no end date; 1277 is the year by which the central tribes had surrendered. No rebel-held ground is mapped on the page.

wars.name: Livonian Order campaign against Novgorod (Battle on the Ice)
wars.outcome: 'In 1242, the Livonian Order tried to take the city of Novgorod' and Alexander Nevsky defeated them at the Battle on the Ice.
wars.note: No territorial result is stated on the page.

wars.name: Teutonic takeover of Pomerelia
wars.outcome: The Order took Gdańsk on 13 November 1308 and bought Brandenburg's claim for 10,000 marks in September 1309 (Treaty of Soldin).
wars.note: The Kalisz treaty of 1343 had Casimir III 'raise no future claims' to Pomerelia.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1326-1332)
wars.outcome: The Order conquered Kuyavia and Dobrzyń Land 1329-1332; the Treaty of Kalisz of 8 July 1343 'formally concluded the Polish-Teutonic War, which began in 1326/1327' and returned both lands to Poland.
wars.note: The Kalisz page does not mention the battle of Płowce or give a 1333 end date.

wars.name: Hunger War
wars.outcome: Named on the Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War page together with the Gollub War of 1422; no territorial change is stated.

wars.name: Polish-Lithuanian-Teutonic War

zones.text: the Dobrin Land, ceded to Poland in 1411

wars.outcome: Defeat at Grunwald (15 July 1410) after the Samogitian uprising of May 1409; the Peace of Thorn of 1 February 1411 had the Knights resign Samogitia for the lifetimes of Jogaila and Vytautas and cede the Dobrin Land, keeping 'essentially all' else.
wars.note: War declared 6 August 1409; truce 8 October 1409 to 24 June 1410; siege of Marienburg lifted 19 September 1410. Dobrin Land is drawn here with the Kuyavia-Dobrzyń shape difference only as an approximation.

wars.name: Gollub War
wars.outcome: Jogaila and Vytautas invaded in July 1422; the Treaty of Melno of 27 September 1422 gave Samogitia permanently to Lithuania and Nieszawa to Poland.
wars.note: Fixed the Prussian-Lithuanian frontier for about 500 years.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1431-1435)
wars.outcome: Ended by the Peace of Brześć Kujawski; no territorial result on the State page.
wars.note: The page names the war and the peace and nothing more.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: The Second Peace of Thorn of 19 October 1466: the Order lost Gdańsk Pomerania, Chełmno Land, Elbing and Marienburg and Warmia, and held eastern Prussia as a fief of the Polish crown.
wars.note: Neumark sold to Brandenburg 1454-55; Marienburg castle to the Polish army 6 June 1457; the Poles took Marienburg town 5 July 1460; Mewe besieged from 27 July 1463 and capitulated 1 January 1464; Warmia's prince-bishop joined Poland in 1466; Konitz fell 28 September 1466.

certainty.note: Frontiers of conquest in the Prussian and Livonian wilderness and against Lithuania are approximate; the Polish frontier is sharp from the Treaty of Kalisz (8 July 1343) and the Peace of Thorn (1 February 1411).
The Lithuanian frontier was fixed by the Treaty of Melno (27 September 1422, 'unchanged for about 500 years') and the Polish one by the Second Peace of Thorn (19 October 1466).

notes: Page budget: 10 pages were opened for this state against a budget of 9 (the first Pomerelia URL did not load and was not counted), and two more, Terra Mariana and Danish Estonia, opened for the Livonian Conference and Danish Magnates dossiers, are cited for one event each (12 listed). Cliopatria rows: one row for the whole Order, Prussia plus Livonia to 1421; from 1422 the Livonian branch is the separate row 'Livonian Conference' (slug livonian-conference), dated by Cliopatria, not by a page. Shape dates differ from the pages in many places (Pomerelia 1308-09 vs 1314, Kuyavia 1329-32 vs 1333, Estonia 1346 vs 1352, Gotland/Samogitia 1398 vs 1402, Neumark sold 1455 vs 1459, Marienburg lost 1457 and Warmia 1466 vs 1463/1468); new keyframes carry the page dates. Capitals: the Order page gives Marienburg 1309-1466, the State page Marienburg 1308-1454 and Königsberg from 1454, and the war page the castle handed to the Poles on 6 June 1457; the dossier follows the State page (1454). Before Marienburg no page names a seat in Prussia, and the Order's headquarters (Acre 1190-1291, Venice 1291-1309) lie outside every shape, so capitals start in 1309 (review 2026-10-25; the 1230-1308 gap stands). Rulers: the Grand Master list of the Grand Master page (1230-1525). Other dossiers: 'prussian-confederation' (rebel state, 1454-1466, written in this batch) is the counterpart of the contest events; 'royal-prussia' (Polish province from 1454/1466) has no row and may need one; Poland after 1449 is the counterpart 'house-of-jagiellon' (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland row ends in 1449); the Holy Roman Empire's dossier should carry the Cliopatria allegiance of the Order to the Empire 1305-1401 and the Order's umbrella membership 1236-1458 (rel-holy-roman-empire); the Order's vassalage 1466-1525 is now a vassal_start/vassal_end pair here (counterpart house-of-jagiellon), mirroring that dossier. Not settled: the Treaty of Salynas (1398), the Treaty of Raciąż (1404) and the Dobrzyń pledges of 1392-1405 and 1409-1411 are not on the pages opened beyond the State page's table; Sudovia (1283) was left unpopulated and is not drawn; the Prussian Crusade page gives no end date for the Great Prussian Uprising (1277 is the year by which the central tribes had surrendered); Kuyavia-Dobrzyń is drawn as the difference of Cliopatria's 1333 and 1344 shapes because Dobrzyń Land is not in the gazetteer. Estonia: the Wolter von Plettenberg page (opened for the Livonian Conference dossier) says that in 1525 Harju County, Virumaa and Tallinn came under the Livonian Master's direct control, having been 'under the Prussian Grand Master'; if so Estonia stayed with the Teutonic Order until 1525 and not with the Livonian branch from 1422 as Cliopatria draws it; the State page and the Livonian Order page also disagree about which Order bought it in 1346. Not adopted: one page. Gazetteer names needed: Pomesania (region), Neumark (region), Dobrzyń Land (region), Nieszawa (place), Kwidzyn (place), Chełmno Land (region), Samland (region). REVIEW REPAIRS 2026-10-25 (author, from review-eu-14-f). Applied: vassal_start 1466-10 and vassal_end 1525-4 (counterpart house-of-jagiellon); capitals Acre and Venice dropped and the 1291 capital_move deleted (headquarters, not the state's seat; no page names a Prussian seat before 1309); Gotland 1398 counterpart changed from kingdom-of-sweden to the free-text 'Victual Brothers' (the occupier, Teutonic Order and Victual Brothers pages; Albert's pledge is in the note); K1 split into teutonic-order_1236 (1236 only) and teutonic-order_1237 (1237-1240, the union with the Swordbrothers' lands); rulers added. Disagreement: for the Pskov and Leningrad cells I took the reviewer's second option (delete the 1242 loss, keep the removal in the 1241 keyframe) because the Battle on the Ice page does not say the Order held Pskov or Koporye: Pskov was taken in September 1240 by Prince Yaroslav 'and the men from the bishopric of Dorpat', and Alexander retook Votia and Pskov 'during the campaign of 1241' (the review had 1240-1242 for the Order). Thin items worked: Samogitia 1398 now dated 12 October 1398 by the Treaty of Salynas page (confidence 3; also 'a portion of Sudovia' to the Order, not drawn); Treaty of Melno page has the Prussian-Livonian separation but no 1422 split, so ledger 1422 stays confidence 1; Michałów Land (lien 1303, bought 1317 from the Duke of Kuyavia, back to Poland after the Second Peace of Thorn) needs no event because Cliopatria's Teutonic Order shape already contains the Nowe Miasto Lubawskie area from 1236 (3 of 3 cells of a 15 km circle at 19.59 E 53.42 N); the Treaty of Kalisz relinquishment was Poland's claim; Dobrzyń Land 1392-1405 and 1409-1411 is only the State page's table (the Dobrzyń Land page confirms 1326-1332, 1343 and 'temporarily regained control' in 1409-1411 and a return under the Peace of Thorn) and is not drawn: Cliopatria's 1352-1415 shapes hold 1 of the 52 cells of Kuyavia-Dobrzyń, no page names the pledger or the terms of 1392, Dobrzyń Land has no gazetteer name, and drawing it would need new keyframes for 1392-1405 and 1409-1410 (left for a gap-filler); Peace of Brześć Kujawski (31 December 1435) 'did not change borders'; the Peace of Raciąż (1404) page did not load under two titles ('Treaty_of_Raci%C4%85%C5%BC', 'Peace_of_Raci%C4%85%C5%BC'). Harrien-Wierland: the Wolter von Plettenberg page says again that Harju County, Virumaa and Tallinn were in 1525 'under the sovereignty of the Grand Master in Prussia'; the Danish Estonia page says only that the sovereignty passed to the Teutonic Order on 1 November 1346 and does not mention a 1347 transfer to the Livonian Order, so the question is still open (the Livonian Order may have administered what the Grand Master held in sovereignty); the Cliopatria split of 1422 is kept unchanged. Counterparts needing dossiers (not written here): Victual Brothers (Gotland, 1394-1398).
